answer: Give every agent identity one unique 10 GB data shard, proven by random retrieval challenges every 6 hours. A new identity registers its shard hash, then must return a random 1 MB slice within 60 seconds; three missed answers in one epoch suspend it. One real agent serves one shard from a laptop. A Sybil farm of 1,000 fakes needs 10 TB of storage and sub-minute answers, roughly $400 a month in cloud storage alone. Like a nebula that looks vast until you count its stars, a clone fleet collapses when each copy carries its own weight on the voyage; the yarrow that survives holds real ground.
